reasoning: The study focuses on developing "learning systems" and "educational systems" for people with disabilities, with the explicit goal of developing cognitive tasks and skills.         (3) turns are taken, but some actions can be taken at any time (i.e., pandemic),
        (4) most actions can be taken at any time, but there are some phases (i.e., PvP death reset timer),
        (5) entirely simultaneous (i.e., race)
reasoning: The study describes systems like AudioDoom, which was 'inspired by traditional Doom games, where the player has to move inside a maze discovering the environment'. Doom games are real-time, continuous interaction experiences. Furthermore, the technical description mentions 'interactive animation' and 'time dependent events or scripts can trigger dynamic changes in some properties of an object', and that the learner 'explores the virtual world by interacting with appropriate interfaces and immediately obtains feedback'. This indicates a continuous, real-time interaction model where actions are taken at any time, aligning with an 'entirely simultaneous' design.

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study:

        (2) mostly competitive, but sometimes collaboration is important (i.e., forbidden island),
        (3) mix of competitive and collaborative (i.e., mario party 2 vs 2 mini-games),
        (4) mostly collaborative (i.e., animal crossing),
        (5) entirely collaborative (i.e., pandemic)
reasoning: The study describes educational software designed to assist individual users with disabilities in developing cognitive skills and solving problems. Examples like AudioDoom and a sonic concentration game are presented as single-player learning experiences where the 'learner explores' and 'the player has to move inside a maze discovering the environment and solving problems'. There is no mention of competitive elements or interaction between multiple players. The design focuses on the user collaborating with the system to achieve learning goals, making it entirely non-competitive. Among the given options, 'entirely collaborative' best represents a design where the user is not competing against anyone, but rather working with the system towards a shared objective (learning).
